tests.title: Unit 2: Introduction to English Composition – Practice Test 1

questions.question_text: Which sentence is the best topic sentence for a paragraph on the benefits of remote work for employees?
options: Remote work offers employees greater flexibility and saves the time spent commuting.
Offices were first built in the nineteenth century in large cities.
The company has 200 employees and three branch offices.
Many people like to eat lunch at home on weekdays.

questions.question_text: A paragraph is said to have unity when:
options: Every sentence begins with a connective
The sentences are of equal length
It contains at least ten sentences
All the sentences relate to a single controlling idea

questions.question_text: Coherence in a paragraph is achieved mainly by:
options: Repeating the first sentence of the paragraph at the very end
Logical order and transitions that link the sentences together
Using only short sentences throughout the whole paragraph
Using as many long and difficult words as the writer can think of

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a transitional word that shows contrast?
Which of the following is a transitional word that shows result?
Which of the following is a transitional word that shows addition?
Choose the best transition: "The product was cheaper than its rivals; ___, its quality was poor."
Choose the best transition: "The server crashed twice on Monday; ___, the clients lost the data."
The concluding sentence of a paragraph should:
options: Repeat each detail in the paragraph
Sum up the main idea or give a closing thought

questions.question_text: The thesis statement of an essay is usually placed:
options: In the middle of the body
At the beginning of the conclusion
At the end of the introduction

questions.question_text: A good thesis statement is:
options: A specific and arguable claim that the essay will support
A list of the sources which the writer has used in the essay
A general fact that no reader would dispute or question
A question for which the essay offers no answer at all

questions.question_text: Which of these is the best thesis statement for an essay?
options: Social media is a thing which is used by a very large number of people today.
This essay is going to be about social media and the students.
Social media harms students' concentration, so schools should limit its use during study hours.
Social media sites were first started by some companies in the early 2000s.

questions.question_text: The body paragraphs of an essay are meant to:
options: Develop and support the thesis with evidence and explanation
Introduce the topic to the reader in a general manner
List the references used by the writer at the end of the essay
Apologise to the reader for the length of the essay

questions.question_text: The conclusion of an essay should:
options: Ask the reader for the permission to publish the essay
Restate the thesis and sum up the key points without a new argument
Quote a long passage from one of the sources used
Present a new argument which has not been discussed earlier

questions.question_text: An essay on "The impact of automation on jobs" that gives arguments both for and against and then reaches a verdict is a(n):
An essay that explains how to prepare a budget, step by step, is a(n):
An essay recounting a personal experience in time order is a(n):
An essay that uses vivid sensory details to portray a place is a(n):
The chronological order of paragraph organisation arranges the details by:
Arranging the details of a paragraph from the least to the most important is called:
The format of a formal business letter includes the sender's address, date, inside address, salutation, body, complimentary close and:
If you begin a business letter with "Dear Sir," you should close it with:
If you begin a business letter with "Dear Mr Sharma," you should close it with:
The subject line of a business e-mail should be:
Which is the most professional opening for an e-mail to a client you have never met?

tests.title: Unit 2: Introduction to English Composition – Practice Test 2

questions.question_text: Which closing is most appropriate in a formal business e-mail?
The tone of a formal business e-mail should be:
Which sentence is the most appropriate in a formal complaint letter?
options: Your company is the worst company that I have ever dealt with.
I am writing to bring to your attention that the goods delivered on 5 March were damaged.
You people are totally useless, and you sent me broken stuff again.
I demand an apology right now or else I will go to the press.

questions.question_text: A memo is generally used for:
options: Communication with customers outside the firm

questions.question_text: The heading of a memo typically includes:
A letter of inquiry is written to:
options: Accept an order placed by a customer for the goods
Apologise for a delay in the delivery of the goods
Request information about the products or services of a firm
Complain about defective goods received from a supplier

questions.question_text: A letter placing an order should clearly mention:
options: Quantity, description, price, delivery date and payment terms
Only the date of the letter and the reference number
Only the name of the buyer and his address
Only the complaint which the buyer has about the last order

questions.question_text: A letter of apology for a delay in delivery should:
options: Avoid any mention of the delay in the delivery of the goods
Offer no solution to the customer for the delay caused
Blame the customer for the delay in the delivery of the goods
Express regret, explain briefly and state the corrective action

questions.question_text: A cover letter accompanies:
options: A résumé or a curriculum vitae

questions.question_text: The first paragraph of a cover letter should:
options: Criticise the previous employer for the reasons of leaving
State the position applied for and how the writer learned of it
List all the previous salaries drawn by the writer in the past
Repeat the résumé of the applicant word for word

questions.question_text: A résumé differs from a CV in that a résumé is generally:
options: A concise one- or two-page summary tailored to a job
A detailed multi-page document of the entire academic career

questions.question_text: The "career objective" or "summary" section of a résumé should be:
options: A long life story of the applicant
A copy of the job advertisement
Brief and tailored to the job being applied for

questions.question_text: Which of the following should NOT be included in a résumé?
options: Irrelevant personal details such as the religion and the parents' income
Education and qualifications of the applicant
Skills and achievements of the applicant

questions.question_text: An effective résumé uses action verbs such as:
A notice is a:
options: Formal announcement to a group of people

questions.question_text: A notice should carry the:
options: Name of every one of the readers of the notice
Telephone number of every one of the readers of the notice
Issuing body's name, date, heading, content and the issuer's signature
Photograph of the writer of the notice

questions.question_text: An agenda for a meeting lists:
options: The items to be discussed, in the order they will be taken up
The decisions which have already been taken at the meeting
The attendance of the members at the previous meeting only
The expenses which have been incurred for the meeting

questions.question_text: The minutes of a meeting record:
options: The personal opinions of the minute-taker
The decisions taken and the actions assigned
Every word spoken by each person

questions.question_text: Minutes of the meeting are written in the:
A business report is:
options: A structured document that presents facts and analysis on an issue
A letter of complaint written to a supplier of the goods
A personal diary which the manager keeps about his daily work
An advertisement for the company in the newspaper

questions.question_text: The usual sequence of a formal report is:
options: Findings, conclusion, title page, summary, introduction
Introduction, title page, recommendations, summary, findings
Recommendations, title page, findings, introduction, summary
Title page, summary, introduction, findings, conclusion, recommendations

questions.question_text: The executive summary of a report is:
options: A list of the references which have been used in the report
A detailed discussion of the methodology of the research only
A short overview of the purpose, findings and recommendations
An appendix of the raw data collected for the report

questions.question_text: The recommendations section of a report should:
options: Suggest specific actions that follow from the findings
Repeat the introduction of the report once again in full
Contain only the raw data collected by the researcher
Criticise the readers who have asked for the report

questions.question_text: An appendix to a report is used for:
options: The main argument which the report presents to the readers
The title of the report and the name of the writer
The conclusion which the report has drawn from the findings
Supporting material such as questionnaires and detailed tables

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a primary source of data for a report?
options: A survey conducted by the writer

tests.title: Unit 2: Introduction to English Composition – Practice Test 3

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a secondary source of data?
options: An observation made by the writer
An interview done by the writer

questions.question_text: Plagiarism means:
options: Paraphrasing an idea and then citing the source in the text
Quoting a source in a proper manner with a full citation
Presenting another person's words or ideas as your own without credit
Summarising a work in a short form and giving credit to the author

questions.question_text: To avoid plagiarism, a writer should:
options: Translate the text and claim that it is the writer's own work
Copy the text and delete the name of the author from it
Cite the sources and put borrowed words in quotation marks
Change a few of the words and not mention the source at all

questions.question_text: A paraphrase is:
options: A short title that is given to the original text by the writer
A restatement of an idea in your own words, with the source acknowledged
A translation of the original text into another language
An exact copy of the original text placed in quotation marks

questions.question_text: A summary differs from a paraphrase in that a summary is:
options: A word-for-word copy of the original, with the quotation marks
About the same length as the original, with the words changed
A condensed version of the main points, much shorter than the original
An addition to the original text, with the comments of the writer

questions.question_text: A précis of a passage is usually about what fraction of the original?
The title of a précis should be:
options: Short and reflect the central idea of the passage
As long as the précis itself
A copy of the first sentence of the passage

questions.question_text: A précis should be written in:
options: The third person, in indirect speech, in the past or the present tense
The second person, in a style that addresses the reader
The first person, in the future tense, in a personal style
Direct speech, with the quotations from the original passage

questions.question_text: The ideal length of a paragraph in a formal essay is:
options: Long enough to develop one idea fully, usually five to eight sentences
A whole page without any break, so that the idea flows
A single sentence, so that the reader is not bored by it
Exactly three sentences in every case, whatever the idea

questions.question_text: A run-on error in a paragraph can be corrected by:
options: Deleting all the commas from the sentence in the paragraph
Adding more clauses to the sentence without any punctuation
Using proper punctuation or a conjunction between the clauses
Writing the whole sentence in capital letters for clarity

questions.question_text: Which sentence uses the semicolon correctly?
options: The meeting ended; late everyone was tired.
The meeting ended late; everyone was tired.
The meeting; ended late everyone was tired.
The meeting ended late; and everyone was tired.

questions.question_text: Which sentence uses the colon correctly?
options: The report: has three parts the introduction, the findings and the conclusion.
The report has three parts the introduction: the findings and the conclusion.
The report has three parts: the introduction, the findings and the conclusion.
The report has: three parts the introduction, the findings and the conclusion.
questions.explanation: Colon after an independent clause introducing a list.

questions.question_text: Which sentence uses the apostrophe correctly?
options: The employees lounge's is on the second floor.
The employees's lounge is on the second floor.
The employee's lounge is for all the employees on the second floor.
The employees' lounge is on the second floor.

questions.question_text: Which sentence uses commas correctly?
options: After the meeting we had, lunch with the clients.
After the meeting we, had lunch with the clients.
After the meeting, we had lunch with the clients.
After, the meeting we had lunch with the clients.

questions.question_text: Which sentence uses the hyphen correctly?
The correct way to write the date in a formal British-style letter is:
Which of the following is a formal word to replace "get" in "get the approval"?
Which is more formal?
options: We feel bad about telling you.
We are sorry to tell you.

questions.question_text: Choose the best concise version of: "Due to the fact that the machine was broken, we were unable to complete the work."
options: In view of the fact that the machine was broken, we could not complete.
Due to the fact of the machine being broken, we were unable to be able to complete the work.
The machine broke and because of this fact we had been unable to complete.
Because the machine was broken, we could not complete the work.

questions.question_text: Choose the best concise version of: "At this point in time, we are in the process of reviewing the proposal."
options: We are in the process of reviewing now the proposal.
At this point in time, we are reviewing the proposal.
We are now reviewing the proposal.
Right at this moment in time we review the proposal.

questions.question_text: Which sentence uses the active voice for clarity?
options: The audit has been completed by the team.
The audit was completed by the team.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is an example of jargon that should be avoided with a general audience?
options: Leverage synergies to optimise the deliverables
Work together to finish the tasks

questions.question_text: The "you-attitude" in business writing means:
options: Using the word "you" in every sentence
Focusing on the reader's needs and benefits

questions.question_text: Which sentence reflects the you-attitude?
options: I need to finish the refunds first.
We will process the refund when we have the time.
Our policy is to process refunds slowly.
You will receive your refund within five working days.

questions.question_text: A positive tone is shown in:
options: It is impossible to deliver sooner.
Unfortunately, we are unable to deliver earlier.
We will be able to deliver by Friday.

tests.title: Unit 2: Introduction to English Composition – Practice Test 4

questions.question_text: Bad-news letters are usually organised by:
options: Opening with the apology alone and then nothing else
Leaving out the reasons for the bad news from the letter
Opening directly with the bad news and then stopping
Opening with a neutral buffer, then the reason, the bad news and a positive close

questions.question_text: Good-news messages are usually organised by:
options: Delaying the good news to the end
Stating the good news first (direct approach)

questions.question_text: The AIDA formula in persuasive writing stands for:
In a sales letter, the "Desire" stage is created by:
options: Describing the history of the company in some detail
Giving the address of the shop in a prominent place
Listing the price of the product on the first line only
Showing how the product meets the reader's needs and benefits him

questions.question_text: The "Action" stage of AIDA is achieved by:
options: Repeating the attention-getter used at the start of the message
Leaving the reader to decide what to do on his own
Ending the message with a joke to leave a good mood
Telling the reader what to do next and making it easy to do

questions.question_text: A proposal is a document that:
options: Reports an event that has taken place in the past
Offers a plan or a solution and seeks approval or funding
Complains about a product that has been bought
Records the minutes of a meeting that has been held

questions.question_text: Which of the following should be avoided in business writing?
options: Short paragraphs that are easy for the reader to follow
Clear headings that guide the reader to the sections
The active voice in the sentences that are written
Slang and abbreviations such as "gonna" and "btw"

questions.question_text: The "inverted pyramid" style of writing places:
options: The details first and the summary last
The conclusion last and the introduction first always

questions.question_text: Proofreading should be done:
options: Before writing the draft, to plan the content of the document
After writing, to check the spelling, grammar and punctuation
Only by the printer, after the document has been printed
Never, since the software does the work for the writer

questions.question_text: Which spelling is correct?
Which spelling is correct?
Which spelling is correct?
Which spelling is correct?
Which spelling is correct?
Which spelling is correct?
Choose the correct word: "The (affect/effect) of the policy on sales was positive."
Choose the correct word: "Please send the document (to/too/two) me."
Choose the correct word: "(Their/There/They're) going to attend the seminar."
Choose the correct word: "The company lost (its/it's) licence."
Choose the correct word: "I would (of/have) attended if I had known."
Choose the correct word: "Fewer/Less: There were ___ complaints this month than last month."
Choose the correct word: "Fewer/Less: We have ___ time than we need."
Choose the correct word: "(Who's/Whose) report is this?"
Choose the correct word: "He is taller (then/than) his brother."
Choose the correct word: "The (principal/principle) reason for the loss was poor planning."
